title: Hurst
name: Hurst
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Hurst, TX investors, covering older Mid-Cities retail and office parcels where title history and permit records need closer review.

sections.html: Hurst sits at the interchange of SH 26 and TX-183, the retail spine of the Mid-Cities that grew up around North East Mall starting in the 1970s. An exchange buyer moving proceeds into Hurst is usually looking at commercial stock that is decades old, and a coordination plan built for newer product elsewhere in Tarrant County will miss the title and permit questions that older Hurst parcels tend to raise. Documentation quality, alongside price, is what separates a clean Hurst closing from one that stalls in the final weeks of a 180-day window.

sections.heading: Why Hurst's Age Changes The Documentation Work
sections.html:
Much of the retail and office inventory fronting SH 26 and TX-183 in Hurst was developed alongside or shortly after North East Mall, which means original recorded easements, cross-access agreements, and reciprocal parking arrangements from that era are still active on many parcels. A title commitment that does not trace those recorded instruments back to the original development plat can miss a restriction that affects redevelopment or signage rights.

Pipeline Road and the smaller office nodes off it were built out in a similar window, and several buildings have gone through at least one prior ownership transfer without an updated survey. Confirming boundary and easement lines with a current ALTA survey, rather than relying on the seller's file copy, is standard practice for a Hurst identification candidate.

A number of these older buildings have also seen partial interior renovations over the years without a corresponding update to the recorded site plan on file with the city, which means a floor plan pulled from county records may no longer match the building as it stands. Confirming current interior configuration against the certificate of occupancy is a reasonable step before a Hurst candidate is formally identified.

sections.heading: Property Types That Actually Trade In Hurst
sections.html:
The Hurst commercial base breaks down into a narrower set of recognizable categories, and knowing which one a candidate falls into shapes the diligence list before it goes on the 45-day identification form.

  • freestanding retail and restaurant pads along SH 26 and TX-183
  • small multi-tenant office buildings off Pipeline Road
  • junior anchor and shop space tied to the mall corridor
  • self-storage and light-service buildings on secondary streets

sections.heading: Where A Generic Exchange Scope Misses Hurst
sections.html:
A quote written from a template usually assumes a clean title history and a recent certificate of occupancy, which is not a safe assumption for buildings built in the mall-corridor boom years. A scope for Hurst should call out a Phase I environmental review as a named line item rather than an optional add-on, particularly for any parcel with a documented prior automotive, dry-cleaning, or fueling use, since those uses are common along older commercial strips in this corridor.

It should also name the step of requesting the municipality's full permit and code-compliance history for the building, alongside the current CO, since older retail centers sometimes carry open permits or unresolved code items from a tenant buildout years earlier. A scope that stops at the CO alone leaves a gap a lender's underwriter is likely to ask about later in the process.

sections.heading: Coordination Sequence For A Hurst Closing
sections.html:
Once a Hurst candidate is under contract, the qualified intermediary should be notified immediately so exchange funds are positioned correctly ahead of the identification deadline, and the lender's underwriting file should include the ALTA survey, title commitment, and permit history before the property is placed on the 45-day list rather than after. Coordinating those three items early gives the closing team room to resolve any recorded easement question without putting the exchange timeline at risk.

Title, lender, and the investor's tax advisor should all confirm receipt of the same document set in writing, since a Hurst closing that relies on informal email confirmation is more likely to miss a discrepancy between the recorded easement language and the current survey until it is too late to correct before day 180.

sections.heading: What The Identification File Should Contain
sections.html: A complete Hurst identification file documents the recorded easements and cross-access agreements tied to the parcel, the certificate of occupancy alongside the permit and code-compliance history, a current ALTA survey, and, where the prior use warrants it, a Phase I environmental report. Assembling these before the deadline rather than during the exchange period keeps the qualified intermediary's release of funds on schedule.

faqs.q: Why does an older Hurst retail building need more diligence than newer product elsewhere in Tarrant County?
faqs.a: Many Hurst parcels along SH 26 and TX-183 were platted during the North East Mall build-out and still carry original recorded easements and cross-access agreements. Confirming those instruments trace correctly to the current parcel is part of standard title review for this corridor.

faqs.q: Is a Phase I environmental report always required for a Hurst identification candidate?
faqs.a: It depends on the property's use history. A parcel with a documented prior automotive, fueling, or dry-cleaning use should carry a Phase I report as a named diligence item rather than an optional extra.

faqs.q: What permit records should be pulled before closing on a Hurst property?
faqs.a: Request the certificate of occupancy plus the municipality's full permit and code-compliance history for the building, since older centers sometimes carry unresolved items from a prior tenant buildout that a current CO alone would not reveal.

faqs.q: When should the qualified intermediary be notified about a Hurst candidate?
faqs.a: As soon as the property goes under contract, so exchange funds are positioned correctly and the 45-day identification deadline and 180-day exchange period stay on track.

faqs.q: What kinds of properties are actually available to buy in Hurst?
faqs.a: Freestanding retail and restaurant pads along SH 26 and TX-183, small multi-tenant office buildings off Pipeline Road, mall-adjacent junior anchor space, and self-storage or light-service buildings on secondary streets make up most of what trades.
